assessment: The paper does report two mutually exclusive analytical pore-length assumptions under one constant alpha_0 construction: every pore has fixed length lambda_0 versus pore lengths drawn from an exponential distribution with scale ell_0. That source pair is scientifically real. The exact ScienceCard presented here is nevertheless not source-closed or executable: it reverses the meaning of alpha_0, invents a finite x domain, units, and parameter values, leaves every numerical p(x) response dependent on unbound symbolic quantities, and treats an exact discrete mass function in the fixed-length branch as the same continuous density used in the exponential branch outside the stated asymptotic limit. Its own selected source ambiguity records the missing parameterization. The card must therefore fail closed rather than proceed to matched-case drafting.

issues.detail: The source defines alpha_i as the probability that a colloid does not dive when entering a pore, i.e. the per-pore flight-survival probability; 1-alpha is the probability of diving. The card repeatedly defines alpha_i/alpha_0 as the diving rate. That reverses the physical meaning of the parameter even though the algebraic factors alpha_0^n(1-alpha_0) use the source's survival-probability convention.

The source never supplies flight_distance_x in a finite [0,10] domain or in 'arbitrary length units'. For the fixed-length branch, the exact support is x=n*lambda_0 and the continuous density is introduced only for x much greater than lambda_c. For the exponential-length branch, the source states an intermediate ell_0 << x << ell_0/(1-alpha_0) power-law range and exponential decay only after the characteristic distance; it does not support the card's common 0-to-10 query range. The branch-B locator support also incorrectly paraphrases line 443 as saying x>ell_0 is the exponential-decay domain.

The card assigns value 1.0 to both lambda_c_constant_pore and decay_length_exp_pore. The cited source gives only lambda_c=-lambda_0/ln(alpha_0) and ell_0/(1-alpha_0); it supplies no numerical alpha_0, lambda_0, ell_0, or numerical decay length for these two subsections. The value 1.0 is therefore not supported by either locator.

The proposed public interface exposes only x and requests p(x), while both branch responses require alpha_0 and a pore-length scale that have neither source-fixed numerical values nor public-control definitions in this card. Consequently the Oracle cannot return a unique objective number for any x from the selected material. The card's linked source_ambiguity explicitly acknowledges this missing parameterization, so the selected cluster would also be rejected by the unresolved-ambiguity gate.

In the fixed-pore branch the exact source result is a delta comb with probability masses at x=n*lambda_0; exp(-x/lambda_c)/lambda_c is only the large-x continuum approximation. In the exponential-pore branch p(x) is a continuous density for x>0 plus a delta mass at zero. Defining both simply as one 'probability density function' over the invented common x interval loses this discrete-versus-continuous distinction and applies branch A outside its stated approximation. A common characteristic-decay statistic could avoid that mismatch, but it is not the readout encoded in this ScienceCard.

review_material.assessment: The source provides a complete derivation of the flight-size PDF for two regimes: constant pore length and exponentially distributed pore length, both with constant diving rate. These regimes share the same control (flight distance x) and readout (flight-size PDF p(x)), and each yields a quantitative exponential decay law with a characteristic length. The cluster is supported by the supplement lines 370-443. The main-text model (variable diving rate, Gamma-distributed pore lengths) is not selected per the routing hint. The extracted evidence supports a numeric control (x), a numeric readout (p(x)), a quantitative mechanism (exponential decay), and an objective response within an explicit domain, so case_authoring_ready is true.

review_material.paper_scope: The paper develops an alternated continuous-time random walk (A-CTRW) model for colloid filtration in a heterogeneous porous medium, linking pore-scale flight-dive dynamics to macroscopic deposition profiles and breakthrough curves. The supplement derives the flight-size PDF under different pore-length and diving-rate assumptions. The selected cluster focuses on the two constant-diving-rate regimes: constant pore length and exponentially distributed pore length.
